subject: A weird LOD peak when using “hk” method

messages.author: a88e586574ebf833
messages.subject: A weird LOD peak when using “hk” method
parts:
Dear all,

I’m using a F7 population with 23k GBS markers to map QTLs.
The GBS markers were imputed by FILLIN algorithm in TASSEL 5.

 

When I used “scanone” with Haley-Knott regression method, I detected a LOD peak in chromosome 3.

But this peak didn’t appear when I used EM method and marker regression method.

 

Is there any possible reason for this situation?

 

 

I attached a part of my data (genotype of chr3 and phenotype) and my R code below

 

Thank you




data <- read.cross(format = "csv", file =  "23kGBS.csv", genotypes = c("AA","AB","BB"),

                      alleles = c("A","B"), estimate.map = F, crosstype = "bcsft", F.gen = 7)

ril <- calc.genoprob(data,step=1,error.prob = 0.01,map.function = "kosambi")


ril.s1<-scanone(ril,pheno.col = 2,method = "hk")
operm.ril <-scanone(ril,pheno.col = 2,method = "hk",n.perm = 1000,n.cluster = 1)
emril.s1 <-scanone(ril,pheno.col = 2,method = "em")
mrril.s1 <-scanone(ril,pheno.col = 2,method = "mr")

par(mfrow = c(3,1))
plot(ril.s1, ylim = c(0,7), main = "Using Haley-Knott Regression")
abline(h = summary(operm.ril,alpha=c(0.01,0.05,0.1)))
plot(emril.s1, ylim = c(0,7), main = "Using EM method")
plot(mrril.s1, ylim = c(0,7), main = "Using Marker Regression")

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] A weird LOD peak when using “hk” method
parts:
There are a very small proportion of heterozygous genotypes, but when read into R/qtl, they are being treated as an F2 intercross. Haley-Knott doesn't work well in this case.

I think it's best to omit the heterozygous genotypes and treat it as RIL by selfing, in which case the peak from Haley-Knott regression goes away.

Either include

crosstype="riself"

in the call to read.cross(), or use

data <- convert2riself(data)

after having read the data into R.

karl
